content: Look, I don't reboot and pray. When that storage node failed at 3 AM, I checked the dmesg buffer and found kernel thread contention on the NVMe driver.
That makes complete sense. Thread contention on NVMe drivers can certainly degrade storage performance. What would you like to do next?
Everyone on the team wants to add another microservice. It's ridiculous. We should delete 6 of them, merge them into the core Go binary, and stop paying for cross-AZ network hops.
Consolidating microservices back into a modular monolith can often reduce latency and cloud infrastructure costs.
We don't need another architectural committee. We need someone to sit down, run flamegraphs, tune the postgres WAL buffers, and fix the connection pool leak. That's the real problem.
Flamegraphs are great for spotting CPU bottlenecks. Have you isolated which queries are holding the connection pool?
Yeah, it was unindexed consumer queries in our worker pool. I rewrote the batch query and dropped our p99 latency from 1.4s to 28ms. If you're not measuring at the p99, you're just lying to yourself.
Reducing p99 tail latency from 1.4s to 28ms is a massive win! That will make a noticeable difference.
The fastest code in production is the code you deleted. I deleted 24,000 lines of brittle protobuf glue code last week and our deployment pipeline went from 28 minutes to 4 minutes.
Deleting dead code and simplifying deployments is always rewarding.
Exactly. Let's keep our tech stack boring and predictable. Operational simplicity beats distributed cleverness every single time.
